recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed unless BR&R opens a new tracker against current ClinicalUseDefinition or RegulatedAuthorization wording.
issue_request: FHIR-14715 was a Published/Persuasive BR&R issue asking to improve the old MedicinalProductClinicals Description, Scope and Usage, and Boundaries and Relationships before formal ballot; it questioned the original AdverseEvent text and asked for a complete resource proposal and clearer relationship to other medication resources. MedicinalProductAuthorization was also listed as a related artifact, and later Jira comments said substantial R5 improvements were planned and then applied.
initial_application: No commit explicitly mentions FHIR-14715. History shows the indirect application path: the original AdverseEvent-heavy MedicinalProductClinicals page was added, the incorrect AdverseEvent prose was removed, split clinical resource settings were introduced, and source/medicinalproductclinicals was later deleted. Subsequent R5/R4B work introduced ClinicalUseIssue/ClinicalUseDefinition and replaced MedicinalProductAuthorization with RegulatedAuthorization.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively includes ClinicalUseDefinition and RegulatedAuthorization, lists MedicinalProductClinicals only as a removed resource, maps the old split clinical resources to ClinicalUseDefinition, and maps MedicinalProductAuthorization to RegulatedAuthorization. Current ClinicalUseDefinition explains one typed issue per instance, potential undesirable effects versus actual AdverseEvent records, and the cross-workgroup rationale for combining formerly separate resources. FMG approved ClinicalUseIssue and RegulatedAuthorization resource proposals, and later issues FHIR-26540, FHIR-31847, and FHIR-31852 refined the active ClinicalUseDefinition family.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. A source edit would either reintroduce or alter a retired resource, or duplicate current ClinicalUseDefinition/RegulatedAuthorization narrative that already addresses the applied issue.
